decisions.reason: Allowing JLCPCB Advanced components where Basic alternatives are unsuitable enables sourcing but does not change the required connector placement, orientation, clearance, or accessibility.
The component-tier policy does not change the required sensor connector fanout, connector types, or individual-cable consolidation policy.
The source changes component sourcing flexibility but does not alter I2C speed, pull-up values, resistor topology, or population policy.
The BOM must still be assembly-ready and contain correct part numbers; accepting Advanced components does not itself change any current BOM-readiness attribute.
Legacy interboard alignment was already eliminated under the integrated-board architecture, and the Advanced-component decision creates no further change.
The requirement for a correct sensor-board BOM remains unchanged; the source does not identify any sensor-board BOM entry requiring modification.
The sourcing-tier decision does not change the required battery protection controller, cutoff behavior, or protection components and functions.
The project remains a single integrated board; permitting Advanced components does not modify board count or architecture.
The source does not change USB data lines, programming behavior, or the requirement for a standard sourceable connector.
Component sourcing tier does not change the requirement that the inductor footprint resolve in KiCad and match the planned physical part.
The legacy main-board BOM requirement does not specify Basic-only components, and the source does not identify a particular unresolved BOM item affected by the policy change.
The required sensor-board fabrication and placement exports remain unchanged by the decision to permit Advanced components.
